tagline: Two national forests, one name, and a long climb to the balds.
intro: The Cherohala Skyway runs from Tellico Plains, Tennessee, over the Unicoi Mountains to Santeetlah Gap near Robbinsville, North Carolina, climbing from about 900 feet at the Tellico River to more than 5,400 feet near the state line. The name joins the Cherokee and the Nantahala, the two national forests it crosses.
It was a long time coming. A wagon train of 67 covered wagons set out in 1958 to campaign for the road, and it was dedicated in 1996, at a cost of about $100 million.

moments.title: Haw Knob
moments.text: A 5,472-foot summit on the state line near the skyway's high point, reached on foot by the Benton MacKaye Trail.

moments.title: Hooper Bald
moments.text: A grassy bald at 5,429 feet that was once a private hunting preserve stocked with buffalo, elk and wild boar; descendants of the boar still root in the woods.

moments.title: Joyce Kilmer Memorial Forest
moments.text: An overlook on the skyway looks down on 3,800 acres of old-growth forest named for the poet of "Trees", with an easy two-mile figure-eight trail.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook
